??? quote "Dialogue"

    - Two hundred and twelve. Two hundred and twelve. Forgive me, *Player*, I count heads twice. The herds are closer to town this year than they have ever been, and the near pastures are grazed to the root.
    - Tavi got my word, then, and sent one back. Good. Neither of us will be the first to walk to the other's fire, but the trails are shared whether we like it or not.
    - My mother on a high pasture again, after five years. She scolded the grass for being short and the wind for being cold. I have not seen her so happy since my father was alive.
    - The herds went out past the Boar Runs side and came home with every head counted. Twice. Thank you.
    - The Greywater. It ran through the driest year my mother can remember, and now it is dust. Ennek carried that alone for a summer. I always feared this day. I did not think it would come so quietly.
    - It runs again, thin as a thread, but it runs. My mother walked all the way to the cleft to see it, knees or no knees. Some days a chieftain only has to stand back and watch.
    - Say what you need. I'm listening, and counting.
        - *Choice:* Who are you?
        - *Choice:* What about the Uskari chieftain?
        - *Choice:* Goodbye.
    - Sennu, chieftain of the Tolmach these thirteen years, since old Bekku died. I lead from a hide tent like any herder, and I move the camps when the grass says so. Mabbu is my mother, Harra my sister, Ennek my son.
    - Tavi and I share the trails and not much else. Tavi wants the herds kept close; I need them on the high pastures. Neither of us will walk to the other's fire first. That is pride, and I know it, and I still won't.
    - Tavi walks the worst stretch personally, I will say that. If the high pasture is safe, Tavi's people and you made it so. I may even say it to Tavi's face. At the next gathering. Possibly.
    - Count your steps on the ledges, *Player*.
